correctness.rationale: PASS: For the fixed marked vertex v in G(n,p), p=1-c log(n)/n with c>0, the event that its neighborhood is a clique and deg(v)=d has exact mass w(n,d)=binom(n-1,d) p^[d(d+1)/2] (1-p)^(n-1-d). All edge factors are independent and no global graph requirement is imposed. Uniformly in a=d/n, log w/(n log n)= -[1-a+(c/2)a²]+o(1), since log binom(n-1,d)=O(n) and log(1-p)=-log n+O(log log n). Laplace principle yields P(v simplicial) exponent Phi(c)=min_{a∈[0,1]}[1-a+c a²/2], equal c/2 for c<=1 and 1-1/(2c) for c>1. Conditional full LDP rate I_c(a)=1-a+c a²/2 - Phi(c), with unique minimizer min(1,1/c), including c=1 boundary. Given the chosen neighbor set, all nonforced edges remain independent with p→1. A uniform Chernoff plus n union bound shows every other normalized degree tends to one under this conditioning. Independently enumerated every graph for n=3,4,5 at p=2/5,3/4 and matched the exact degree masses; finite tests cannot prove LDP.

value.rationale: PASS: Being simplicial (clique neighborhood) is a fundamental local graph property in chordal elimination. Its rare occurrence under logarithmically sparse missing edges forces a nontrivial trade-off between deleting incident edges and enforcing neighborhood adjacency. The result rigorously locates the sharp c=1 mechanism switch and proves that conditioning dramatically affects only one vertex at macroscopic scale, with an explicit full rate function. This is a natural phase transition, not an arbitrary numerical threshold.
